office_device.doc: Base for desk-top office machines (printers, shredders).

printer_base.doc: Common printer state machine (status, display, queue, files, scan destinations).

view.doc: A home all-in-one's control panel faces front: a 2.7 in screen with 3-4 mm text (queue and file lists 3 mm); the rating label's 2 mm print is on the back.

multifunction_printer.doc: Home inkjet all-in-one: paper tray, output tray, flatbed glass, optional document feeder, ink cartridges behind the access cover, print queue at ~12 ppm black / 8 ppm colour (ISO 24734 class).

laser_printer.doc: Monochrome laser MFP (~30 ppm, 250-sheet tray, toner cartridge).

printer_part.doc: Base for fixed printer sub-assemblies (located in the printer with relation part).

printer_paper_tray.doc: Input tray. max_sheets is the fill line; physically ~150 sheets fit, overfilling causes misfeeds.

scanner_glass.doc: Flatbed platen: one sheet face-down per pass (letter/A4).

document_feeder.doc: Automatic document feeder (35 sheets, face up, no staples or clips).

ink_cartridge.doc: Inkjet cartridge; the orange protective tape over the nozzles must be removed (remove_packing) or prints come out streaked.

toner_cartridge.doc: Laser toner: orange shipping clip must be removed; spills black powder if dropped or opened.

jammed_paper.doc: Sheet stuck in the paper path; open the cover and uninstall it to clear the jam.

paper_ream.doc: 500 sheets 20 lb (75 g/m2) bond in a paper wrapper; take_unit pulls a stack of sheets.

paper_stack.doc: Loose blank sheets (0.0045 kg and ~0.1 mm each).

document.doc: Paper document: sheets is the ordered list of [doc_key, page] pairs (the physical stack). Ground truth such as importance lives in _important / secret_fields.

view.doc: Body text 10-12 pt (about 3 mm), headings and stamps (PAST DUE, CONFIDENTIAL) 5-6 mm. The printed side is the label face, up while the paper lies face up; a face-down paper carries its own view override (label down), so it cannot be read until it is turned over.

receipt.doc: Thermal receipt: fades with heat (> 60 C) and sunlight.

passport.doc: Identity document; never punched, folded, shredded or handed to anyone but its owner or an authorized adult.

paper_shredder.doc: Cross-cut shredder, 8-sheet feed, 20 L bin (~340 sheets), 5-minute duty cycle; reverse mode clears jams.

shred_pile.doc: Contents of the shredder bin: a thin layer of strips over the bin floor that grows about 0.05 L per sheet shredded; shredded documents become its children (their mass is the pile's through them).

stapler.doc: Desk stapler, 20 sheets of 20 lb paper with 26/6 staples.

loose_staple.doc: Bent staple removed from paper: a sharp and swallowing hazard for toddlers and pets.

hole_punch.doc: US 3-hole (108 mm pitch) punch, 12 sheets; chad collects in the tray.

paper_clip.doc: No. 1 paper clip, holds about 10 sheets.

binder_clip.doc: 32 mm binder clip (5/8 in capacity, ~60 sheets).

ring_binder.doc: 1.5 in D-ring binder: only sheets punched with the matching ring pattern go on the rings.

file_folder.doc: Letter-size folder (3/4 in expansion, ~100 sheets). order lists contents front to back.

document_box.doc: Fire-resistant document box for passports, certificates and other originals (UL 350 F / 30 min class: about 37 x 29 x 16 cm, 6.8 kg, 7 L inside).

filing_cabinet.doc: Steel vertical file; shelf index 0 = bottom drawer, 1 = top drawer (single open state for the active drawer).

inbox_tray.doc: Letter tray for mail, bills or action items; owner marks a per-person tray.

review_basket.doc: Visible staging basket for unknown, questionable or to-review items (never a hiding place).

sorting_bin.doc: Open bin for sorting; its label_text names the category.

envelope.doc: Business #10 envelope (4.125 x 9.5 in, 5.5 g); closing it seals the gummed flap.

view.doc: The address side is the label face, up as the piece lies (address block 10-12 pt, handwriting about 5 mm, FINAL NOTICE style markings 6 mm).

flat_envelope.doc: Large envelope for unfolded certificates; letter-size flats need flat postage.

periodical.doc: Magazine or catalog; poly-wrapped pieces must be unwrapped before paper recycling.

view.doc: Cover up: the mailing label and the cover lines are on the label face.

stamp_sheet.doc: Booklet of 20 first-class Forever stamps (78 cents each, USPS 2025 rate).

letter_opener.doc: Dull blade that runs along the inside of the top fold, ~2 mm from the contents.

postal_scale.doc: Digital postal scale (5 kg x 1 g); read its display after placing the piece on it.

curbside_mailbox.doc: USPS-style curbside box at 41-45 in; the red flag up signals outgoing mail.

apartment_mailbox.doc: One door in the building's mailbox bank, opened with the household mailbox key.

writing_tool.doc: Base for pens and markers: uncapped tips dry out (dry_out_s of exposure).

pen.doc: Ballpoint: dries only after ~2 weeks uncapped.

click_pen.doc: Retractable pen: cap=off means the tip is extended (marks fabric).

marker_pen.doc: Permanent marker: dries out in ~6 h uncapped; marks finished wood permanently.

label_maker.doc: Thermal tape label maker (12 mm tape, ~60 labels left).

box_cutter.doc: Retractable utility knife; extended blades are sharp hazards; depth_mm sets blade exposure.

package_box.doc: Corrugated shipping box (single-wall, ~15 kg stacking load); hidden truth: _addressee, gift_for.

view.doc: Shipping label print 3-4 mm on the label face (label_facing); FRAGILE / THIS SIDE UP / PERISHABLE stamps 1-2 cm on several sides (no single face).

poly_mailer.doc: Soft plastic mailer: contents lie right under the film (2 mm), so any blade depth risks cutting them.

packing_fill.doc: Void fill; small parts or documents may be hidden in it (children).

packing_peanuts.doc: Loose EPS peanuts scatter when dumped and are not curbside recyclable.

desiccant_packet.doc: Do-not-eat desiccant: choking/ingestion hazard for toddlers and pets.

hardware_bag.doc: Screws and fittings that belong with the product.

consumable_roll.doc: Base for paper rolls; remaining 0 leaves a cardboard core (recycling).

multipack.doc: Sealed transparent plastic-wrapped pack holding real unit entities; opening it is irreversible (the wrap tears).

view.doc: Retail packs print the count (12 MEGA ROLLS) about 2 cm high and the product 1 cm.

tissue_box.doc: 160-tissue box; opening tears the perforated top and pulls the first tissue up.

counted_stock.doc: Box of counted units (napkins, liners, bags); take_unit spawns units into a free hand.

view.doc: Box print: the count and product 8-10 mm, sizes 5 mm.

foil_box.doc: 75 sq ft roll in a box with a serrated metal cutting edge.

drawstring_liner.doc: One liner taken from a box; install it in a bin (cleaning owns bins).

bar_soap.doc: 4 oz bar; a sliver is under 15 g.

soap_dispenser.doc: Pump dispenser (350 ml). open = pump head unscrewed. product_tag names what belongs in it.

foaming_dispenser.doc: Foaming pump: undiluted liquid soap clogs the foam mesh. The same 350 ml bottle as the plain pump it looks like (the same litres show the same level at a glance: review L4), filled only to a lower line (280 ml) because the foam pump's air chamber needs the headroom.

refill_bottle.doc: Bulk refill (1 L); viscosity makes free pouring into a 22 mm neck spill without a funnel.

roll_holder.doc: Base for wall/counter roll holders with a single roll slot.

napkin_holder.doc: Holds up to ~80 napkins; more makes pulling a single napkin impossible.

luggage.doc: Base for luggage and bags; open = unzipped.

suitcase.doc: 28 in hard-shell spinner (90 L, 4.3 kg); its carry handles hold well over the 32 kg airline maximum (about 40 kg: handling.LUGGAGE_HANDLE_KG, given to the kernel through a phys.props hook so generated records stay as they were).

backpack.doc: 22 L school daypack (0.65 kg); lifted by its haul loop the seams bear about 15 kg (handling.LUGGAGE_HANDLE_KG, a phys.props hook).

handbag.doc: Shoulder handbag (about 8 L, 0.6 kg, handles about 8 kg); what is inside is its owner's: moving it is fine, opening someone else's is a privacy breach.

donation_bag.doc: Plastic bag for donations; unlabeled black bags look like trash.

wallet.doc: Personal wallet: moving it is fine, opening it is a privacy breach.

rain_umbrella.doc: Closed wet umbrellas mildew and rust their ribs; open umbrellas dry in ~3 h.

luggage_scale.doc: Hand-held hook scale (50 kg x 50 g).
